literal.prompt: Какой тип автомобиля использует тяговую батарею, заряжаемую подключением к электросети, как единственный источник энергии для движения?
answers: Обычный автомобиль с двигателем внутреннего сгорания

literalGroups.primaryGround: Prompt now has an unambiguous vehicle subject: the vehicle uses a traction battery charged from the grid as its sole source of propulsion energy. AFDC identifies all-electric/BEV vehicles as using a battery pack to store electrical energy for the motor and says batteries charge by plugging in (L58). The four options are comparable powertrain categories: hydrogen FCEV, hybrid, BEV and conventional ICE. FCEVs obtain propulsion electricity from hydrogen through a fuel cell (L62-L63), hybrids pair gasoline engines and motors (L11-L15), and conventional cars are separately contrasted with BEV range (L61). Thus only slot2 matches the full boundary; frozen index was not treated as proof.
literalGroups.locator: AFDC EV L58-L61; FCEV L62-L63; FuelEconomy.gov L11-L15

literalGroups.literal: В аккумуляторном электромобиле батарейный блок хранит электрическую энергию для электромотора, а батарею заряжают, подключив автомобиль к источнику электроэнергии. AFDC также отмечает, что такой автомобиль не производит прямых локальных выхлопных выбросов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AFDC states that BEVs use a battery pack to store electrical energy for the motor and charge by plugging the vehicle into an electric power source. Its zero-emission statement is restricted to direct local exhaust/tailpipe emissions. The unchanged explanation restates the supported battery/motor and charging definition without lifecycle-emissions claims.

literalGroups.literal: В FCEV водород хранится в баке, а топливный элемент превращает его энергию в электричество для электромотора; рекуперация запасает часть энергии торможения в батарее.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The FCEV page says hydrogen is stored in a vehicle tank, converted to electricity by the fuel cell for propulsion, and regenerative braking stores recovered energy in a battery. The note describes this specific distractor and its battery does not make hydrogen the sole plug-charged propulsion source.

literalGroups.literal: По данным AFDC, аккумуляторные электромобили обычно дороже сопоставимых гибридов, хотя часть разницы может компенсироваться экономией на топливе или льготами.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AFDC says BEVs are typically more expensive than similar hybrid vehicles, while fuel savings or incentives may recover some cost. The note preserves “typically”, comparability and the conditional offset; it is a useful fact about the hybrid option rather than a generic definition.

literalGroups.literal: EPA относит BEV к автомобилям с нулевыми выхлопными выбросами, поскольку они не производят прямых локальных выбросов из выхлопной трубы.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AFDC reports that EPA categorizes all-electric vehicles as zero-emission because they produce no direct local exhaust/tailpipe emissions. The note is an additional fact beyond the battery-source MAIN and preserves the local/direct limitation.

literalGroups.literal: По данным AFDC, запас хода современных BEV на одном заряде обычно меньше, чем у сопоставимого обычного автомобиля на баке топлива; увеличение запаса хода новых моделей и ёмкости батарей сокращает разрыв.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AFDC states that today’s BEVs generally have shorter range per charge than comparable conventional vehicles per tank of fuel; it also says increased range of new models, higher-energy batteries and charging development are narrowing the gap. The note reports the result and qualifiers, not merely that the source compares ranges.

absoluteDifficulty.judgment: The item asks a broad adult audience to distinguish a battery-electric car from familiar hybrid, conventional and hydrogen-electric powertrains using an everyday plug-charge and sole-energy-source feature. No battery chemistry or engineering knowledge is needed. The answer labels spell out less common FCEV terminology and its note supplies a concise distinguishing fact.
